text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: hosted-api-us-west-1 p99 latency > 18s and queue depth rising above 8k for the last 5m. Alert: INC-2026-1287. Paging on-call (Meera Patel).
Meera Patel: ACK'ing. looking at grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.com/d/hosted/queue-overview?panel=7&orgId=1 — queue graph looks like steady climb starting ~10:04 UTC. p95 ~6s, p99 ~22s.
Meera Patel: Anyone on call for infra? I see a lot of PENDING GPU instances during scale up, provisioning API errors 429 in cloud logs.
Alex Chen: I can jump in. noticing autoscaler leader logs show repeated 'scale attempt failed: quotaExceeded' - cloud API rate limits + regional GPU quota hit.
Jordan Kim: Confirmed. gcloud IAM quotas show GPUs available = 0 in us-west-1; requests are hitting ProjectQuotaLimit. Cloud returned 429/403 for most createInstance calls.
Samir Gupta: That's why replicas stuck in PROVISIONING. Workaround: we can route low-priority traffic to fallback model (cpu-quant) to reduce GPU pressure. Is that safe?
Meera Patel: Good idea. Start immediate routing change. @Alex can you open a quick canary route to cpu fallback for non-authenticated and experimental customers?
Alex Chen: On it. running: `redwoodctl routes create --name fallback-cpu-ephemeral --selector "tier:low" --model cpu-quant-v1 --region us-west-1 --weight 100`
Alex Chen: command returned: OK. traffic routing policy applied. Propagation ETA ~30s.
Priya Rao: Noted for support — customer impact: some free-tier/dev orgs will see lower quality but lower latency. I'll post a brief status to #support once we have numbers.
Meera Patel: Also manually scaling GPU pool while we coordinate with cloud. Command: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool hosted-us-west-1-gpu --replicas 6` (trying to pick up any remaining capacity).
Jordan Kim: That returned error: creation requests queued, but cloud API returned 429. Retry backoff in effect.
infra-bot: Autoscaler health: leader=autoscaler-3, last_successful_scale=1715122700, consecutive_failures=18. Error summary: [QuotaExceeded, RateLimitExceeded, InsufficientCapacity].
Samir Gupta: We need to stop unbounded retries that are burning our cloud quota windows. I'll flip autoscaler to 'saturation-protect' mode: reduce concurrency of scale attempts and increase retry interval.
Alex Chen: Made change: `helm upgrade autoscaler --set scale.retryInterval=60s --set scale.maxBurst=1` — new config applied.
Meera Patel: Good. Any chance to free up existing GPU capacity by evicting long-running low-priority tasks? Could prune old in-progress jobs in backlog queue.
Jordan Kim: Running a filter to list jobs by start time: `redwoodctl jobs list --state running --sort start_time --filter "priority:low"` returns ~420 long-running low-priority reqs. Proposing `redwoodctl jobs cancel --filter "priority:low AND running_time>120s"` to free KV caches. Approve?
Alex Chen: Approve. Execute and monitor.
Alex Chen: Executed cancel, ~390 tasks evicted. Queue depth dropped ~12% in next push. p95 improved from 6s -> 4.5s. p99 still high (~14s).
Meera Patel: Good delta. Next: enable request-level throttling to protect critical customers. `feature-flag:priority-throttle` flip for hosted-api. Jordan, can you apply a 30% throttle to anonymous/public callers?
Jordan Kim: Applied throttle rule: `throttle.rule.add --match "auth:anonymous" --rate 70rps --burst 200` — verified via policy list.
Priya Rao: Posting update for customers: "We are mitigating elevated latencies in US-WEST. Low-priority traffic is being routed to a CPU fallback and anonymous request rates are being throttled. Engineers are working on autoscaler retries & cloud quota. No action required from customers at this time." Will post now. :loudspeaker:
Meera Patel: Paging escalation: cloud support case opened (CS-98724). They're investigating quota pool across orgs. Meanwhile, can we enable cross-region failover for new traffic? Route a portion (10%) to eu-west as spillover?
Alex Chen: Creating spillover route: `redwoodctl routes update --name hosted-default --add-spillover region=eu-west-1 weight=10` — success.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1287 updated: severity -> S2 (customer-impacting, degraded latency) — responders: Meera, Alex, Jordan, Samir, Priya.
Samir Gupta: Suggest also switching default model to a smaller fp16-quant model for top-tier customers if p99 doesn't drop in 15m. That reduces GPU time per request by ~35%. Thoughts?
Meera Patel: Let's hold that as a fallback. Deploy the canary config to 5% of traffic for premium customers first. Alex, can you do canary deploy?
Alex Chen: Canary policy applied: premium 5% -> model fp16-compact-canary. Monitoring.
Jordan Kim: Cloud support replied: quota reclaim in flight, ETA ~25-40m. They recommend reducing parallel create attempts. We already throttled retries.
Meera Patel: OK. timeline: if p99 not <10s in 20m, escalate to exec ops and consider emergency contract quota bump. Priya keep customers updated with next update in 15m.
Priya Rao: Will send update in 15. Also opening support tickets for 3 customers who reported 504s: TKT-40321, TKT-40322, TKT-40323.
Alex Chen: Observability: traces show tail latency caused by queue head-of-line blocking from a small set of large-context requests. Implemented transient prefix-caching eviction and set `max_input_tokens=2048` hard cap for anonymous routes.
Jordan Kim: After evictions + throttles + cpu-fallback, queue depth down from 8.2k -> 2.1k over 18 minutes. p95 ~3s, p99 ~8.5s. Still degraded but improving.
Meera Patel: Great progress. I'll start a formal incident doc and assign postmortem owner after we stabilize. For now, maintain the routing and throttles until cloud quota returns.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1287: status=monitoring. Next update scheduled in 15m.
Priya Rao: Posted customer status: https://status.redwood.com/incident/INC-2026-1287 — included mitigations and ETA estimates.
Alex Chen: Handing off to night on-call: @Jordan Kim — please monitor queue and p99; if p99 >12s for next 10m, escalate to S1.
Jordan Kim: ACK. Monitoring. Will escalate if thresholds breach.
Meera Patel: Thanks team — great quick coordination. We'll circle back for postmortem once cloud quota resolves.
